newsitem.title: USA: NCR Corp expects year revs to grow 5-10 pct.
newsitem.headline: NCR Corp expects year revs to grow 5-10 pct.

text.p: NCR Corp said that it expects revenues to begin growing in the second quarter and that full-year revenue growth should be in the range of five to 10 percent.

"With orders we got in the first quarter, on a local currency basis we see (revenue) growth in the five to 10 percent range for the full year," the company's senior vice president and chief financial officer John Giering told analysts in a conference call.
Last year's revenues were about $6.9 billion, he said.

Earlier, the company announced a narrower first quarter loss of $16 million, or $0.16 a share, compared with a loss of $65 million, or $0.64 for the prior year's first quarter. First quarter revenues declined 12 percent from a year ago to $1.39 billion.

Giering said the company's optimistic outlook was based on expected order growth this year of between 10 percent and 20 percent. Order growth increased in the range of zero to five percent in the first quarter, he said.

He said the company had many new customers for its database warehouse products that could be upgraded in the future and cited a tripling of the size of its contract with Wal-Mart Stores Inc and a $9 million contract with the U.S. Army.

Because of the spin-off from AT&T Corp completed at the end of last year, he said NCR would continue to have a high 75 percent tax rate for this year due to the inability to obtain a tax benefit from the company's U.S. losses. Overseas sales accounted for just over half NCR's revenues.

Giering said the company had "no specific plans" for its $1.1 billion in cash on hand, but would consider a small number of smaller acquisitions or a potential dividend. Any stock repurchase would have to wait two years, he said.

Revenues could get a boost if new products gained acceptance, including a process that helps banks process checks more easily and a prototype of a self-service retail checkout scanner due out at the end of the year.
In addition, placements of new automated teller machines, of which NCR is the leading supplier, were expected to grow at a 15 percent rate at non-bank premises.
